previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and diabetes was admitted for persistent substernal chest pain unresponsive to nitroglycerin. Initial evaluation showed no EKG changes or troponin elevation, but due to high cardiac risk and ongoing symptoms, he underwent an exercise stress test that revealed reduced exercise tolerance and symptoms during recovery. A cardiac catheterization confirmed two-vessel coronary disease with a significant blockage in the LAD, leading to placement of a drug-eluting stent and PTCA. He also received an extra hemodialysis session for volume overload and was transfused for anemia. A urinary tract infection with hematuria was treated with antibiotics, and outpatient urology and podiatry follow-ups were arranged for hematuria and a chronic toe ulcer. Blood pressure was managed with uptitrated lisinopril and metoprolol. He was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications and clear follow-up instructions.

## CAD: s/p CABG, DES to LM/Lcx in ___, DES to ___ LAD
___, s/p DES to the ___-LAD ___ p/w story consistent with 
unstable angina resistant to nitrates in the setting of aerobic 
activity. CP resolved with Morphine in the ED and was pain free 
after that time for his entire hospital course. ECG consistent 
with old infarct, but no apparent ST changes. Biomarkers were 
flat. Patient was placed on heparin drip. Given recent multiple 
stent placemets, elected to evaluate with cardiac cath to
